notes.title: BESSELI is ITK's published polynomial and recurrence, on the x87 unit
notes.statement: BESSELI truncates n to an integer and evaluates the body published in ITK with every operation stored from the x87 unit at precision 64: the I0 and I1 polynomials, and for higher orders Miller backward recurrence from j = 2*(n + int(sqrt(40*n))), rescaling by 1E-10 whenever |q| > 1E10, then normalising by I0(x). notes.title: Small arguments take Cody's rational on the x87 unit, and the last bit can be high
notes.statement: For normal x with |x| < 2^-28, ERF.PRECISE computes p = RN53(RN64(x*P0)) and y = RN53(RN64(p/Q0)): x87 precision 64, the product stored to binary64, then the quotient stored to binary64. P0 = 0x3ff1df5e70c7956b and Q0 = 0x3fefada15778ece6. These are A(4) and B(4) of Cody's 1969 rational for |x| <= 0.5 (3.20937758913846947e3 and 2.84423683343917062e3), both divided by one real scale s = 2873.12583276792695. notes.title: MROUND counts a quotient within 5E-15 below a half up
notes.statement: MROUND(n,m) forms q = n/m on the x87 unit, counts floor(q), adds 1 when 0.5 - frac(q) <= 5E-15, and returns count*m from the x87 unit. A number just below a half therefore rounds up though it is nearer the lower multiple: 0.499999999999995 with multiple 1 gives 1, and the next binary64 below it gives 0. MROUND(6.05,0.1) stays 6, because its quotient 60.49999999999999 lies 7.1E-15 below the half.
notes.basis: All 50,782 recorded MROUND rows match this rule. The cut-off lies between the adjacent binary64 values 4.996E-15 (rounded up) and 5.0515E-15 (rounded down) from 0.5, measured at floor(q) = 0 over 4,264 rows.
notes.inferred: The window is measured between two neighbouring values; that the constant is the decimal 5E-15 is inferred, as the decimal in that window.

notes.title: ROUND counts digits in 32 bits, and the count wraps
notes.statement: ROUND cuts num_digits toward zero to a 32-bit integer D, limited to +/-2147483647, and keeps k = D + e + 1 significant digits, where e is the decimal exponent of |number| and the sum is computed in 32 bits. k of 15 or more keeps the 15-digit reading of the number; k below 0 gives 0. A large positive num_digits therefore wraps to no digits at all: for a number near 1.1E14, 2147483617 returns the number and 2147483635 returns 0. The boundaries move by exactly -e on both the +2^31 and -2^31 sides, for e from -308 to 308. num_digits of 2^31 or more acts as +2147483647 and -2^31 or less as -2147483647.
notes.basis: Under the family rules the OxFunc-Evidence bank matches ROUND 36,391 of 36,945 rows, ROUNDUP 49,013 of 52,841, ROUNDDOWN 59,080 of 59,995 and TRUNC 50,409 of 51,317, with no row lost and each remaining failure classified in the write-up. The wrap boundary was read at every decimal exponent in the bank.

notes.title: The rounding functions read 15 digits first, so ROUNDDOWN can round up
notes.statement: Before choosing a digit these functions read the number to 15 significant digits on the x87 unit: with e the decimal exponent and n = 14 - e, y = RN64(|x| * 10^n), or RN64(|x| / 10^-n) when n is negative, while 10^|n| is exact in 64 bits (|n| <= 27). A half in y goes up for ROUNDDOWN, ROUNDUP and TRUNC and down for ROUND. So digits beyond the 15th are lost even when the requested precision keeps them: ROUND(-1594628480062905,14) loses its last digit, and ROUNDDOWN(283025097725723.5,0) returns 283025097725724, larger than its input.

notes.title: ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC read num_digits from its low 16 bits
notes.statement: ROUNDUP, ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC take the digit count from the low 16 bits of the integer part of |num_digits|, with the sign of num_digits. If |num_digits| is 2^32 or more, or those low bits are 32768 or more, the truncation happens at 100 places (10^-100, or 10^100 for a negative count). So 65536 acts as 0, 65537 as 1, 32768 to 65535 as 100, and -2147483748, whose low 16 bits are 100, as -100. In the out-of-range case ROUNDUP adds no unit for a positive count, and gives #NUM! for a negative count when a digit is dropped.
notes.basis: Under the family rules the OxFunc-Evidence bank matches ROUND 36,391 of 36,945 rows, ROUNDUP 49,013 of 52,841, ROUNDDOWN 59,080 of 59,995 and TRUNC 50,409 of 51,317, with no row lost and each remaining failure classified in the write-up. All 13,914 informative ROUNDDOWN and TRUNC rows with large num_digits follow the rule.

notes.title: For bills longer than 182 days TBILLEQ is a quadratic, not the documented formula
notes.statement: When DSM is above 182, TBILLEQ does not use the documented formula. It uses the bond-equivalent quadratic (-t + sqrt(t^2 - (2t-1)(1 - 1/p))) / (t - 1/2), with t = DSM/365 and p = price/100. The square root is taken in extended precision and stored, RN53(RN64(sqrt)); the rest is binary64. For the row below, DSM 203, the documented formula gives 0.244038 and Excel 0.241103. notes.title: TRUNC of DBL_MIN returns a subnormal, not 0
notes.statement: With DBL_MIN (0x0010000000000000) as number, TRUNC, ROUNDDOWN and ROUNDUP return the subnormal 0x000ffffffffffffa at each num_digits recorded, so TRUNC(DBL_MIN,0) is not 0. That value is 6 steps below DBL_MIN and 3 steps below 0x000ffffffffffffd, the binary64 nearest the 15-digit reading 2.22507385850720E-308. The bank holds 256 such rows for each of the three functions.
